- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.40) and forecast is trending down, model often undercorrects — increase forecast slightly to avoid premature bearish bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+1.5% from prior day), model tends to overshoot and overcorrect — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% in next 3–5 days to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is positive and forecast is flat or slightly rising, model often underestimates upward momentum — raise forecast by 0.3–0.8% for next 3–7 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in the 10–15 day horizon when sentiment is negative — apply +0.5–1.0% bias to forecast for that window.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often fails to capture mean reversion — adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average if deviation > 0.7% from recent history.  
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in the first 5 days of the 30-day window — apply +0.3–0.6% upward bias to early days if sentiment is negative.
